declarations.name: Causal.Causality.mapsTo_inside_of_boundaryChart
declarations.statement: [T2Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] → hS : C.IsCauchySurfaceOn W S → hC : C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W → hcaus : (∀ ⦃x y : M⦄, C.le W x y → C.le W y x → x = y) → hVW : V ≤ W → hVJ : ↑V ⊆ C.Jminus W S → hfr : (∀ x ∈ (↑U ∩ closure ↑V) \ ↑V, x ∉ W) → C.CausalCurveOn U c a b → c a ∈ V → MapsTo c (Icc a b) ↑V
declarations.standing: Deliverable (1), the curve form, under the target's proposed name, for the past boundary chart (U is Sbierski's Ũ). Proof: τ = sInf (Icc a b ∩ c⁻¹' Vᶜ), the first exit time (closed by ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed, attained by IsClosed.csInf_mem). a < τ, c lies in V on [a, τ), and c τ ∈ (U ∩ closure V) ∖ V (ContinuousWithinAt.mem_closure, closure_Ico), so c τ ∉ W. Over [a, τ), c is a future-inextensible causal curve of W (futureInextensible_of_leaving, with the larger open W ⊔ U, T2). Its point c a ∈ V ⊆ J⁻(S, W) gives t₀ ∈ [a, τ) with c t₀ ∈ S (FutureInextensible.exists_mem_of_mem_Jminus). For t ∈ [t₀, τ), c t ≤_W s for some s ∈ S, and c t₀ ≤_W c t ≤_W s, so c t₀ = s (IsCauchySurfaceOn.eq_of_le_of_t1_secondCountable) and c t = c t₀ by antisymmetry. So c τ ∈ closure {c t₀} = {c t₀} ⊆ W, a contradiction. V disjoint from S is not used.

findings: No defect in Sbierski's text. (2.4) and its proof (sbierski2023c.txt:352–358) are correct as printed. His sentence 'does not intersect Σ' rests on I⁺(Σ) ∩ Σ = ∅, which holds because a Cauchy hypersurface is achronal. In ETT ≪ is not irreflexive by axiom, so the formal proof replaces that step: once the curve meets S it is constant, so it cannot reach the frontier.

About the target's statement, not the paper: 'V disjoint from S' is not needed. The curve meets S at some t₀ < τ. For t ∈ [t₀, τ), c t ∈ V ⊆ J⁻(S, W) gives c t ≤_W s ∈ S, and c t₀ ≤_W c t ≤_W s, so c t₀ = s (S is acausal, IsCauchySurfaceOn.eq_of_le_of_t1_secondCountable) and c t = c t₀ (antisymmetry). Then continuity gives c τ = c t₀ ∈ W, which contradicts c τ ∉ W. So the I⁻ corollary the evidence allowed under 'irreflexivity of ≪_W on S' holds with no extra hypothesis (mapsTo_inside_of_boundaryChart_of_Iminus).
About the target's statement: the curve form needs only V ≤ W, not V ≤ W ⊓ Ũ. V ≤ Ũ is used only in the relation forms, where a curve of Ũ lying in V is restricted to V.

Sharpness, formalized on the timelike line. The frontier hypothesis cannot be dropped (timelikeLine_boundaryChart_needs_frontier: Ũ = ]-1, 2[, and the frontier point 1 lies in W). Nor can V ⊆ J⁻(S, W) (timelikeLine_boundaryChart_needs_Jminus: W = V = ]-1, 1[, S = {0}, Ũ = ]-2, 2[). The relation forms are one-sided: I⁻(1/2, Ũ) ⊄ I⁻(1/2, V) in the witness.
questions: Reading 1, the objects (the reading of Causal.C0ExtensionSkeleton, OQ-154, not decided here). Sbierski's M̃ is M with the one causality C. ι(M) is the open W. His I^±(·, Ũ) and causal curves 'in Ũ' are the relations and curves of the open U. The time orientation of Ũ (∂₀ future-directed, 'agrees with the induced time orientation of M below the graph', :348–349) is built into the single causality C, as OQ-115 reads M̃ time-oriented for the C⁰ skeleton. 'Below the graph of f' is V, and the graph is the frontier of V in Ũ. So (2.3) becomes 'no point of (Ũ ∩ closure V) ∖ V lies in W'. Showing that a C⁰ boundary chart has these properties is layer 3 (T-loc-c0-past-boundary-chart).

Reading 2, 'Cauchy hypersurface' (:329) is read as DEC-14's IsCauchySurfaceOn: every inextensible causal curve meets S exactly once. This is the library's standing reading, as in T-abs-past-inextensible-meets-cauchy. One layer-3 caveat. If Sbierski's Σ is a Lorentzian Cauchy hypersurface in the timelike sense (met exactly once by every inextendible timelike curve) and contains a null segment, it is not DEC-14 Cauchy. Then the Lean applies only after Σ is replaced by an acausal Cauchy hypersurface S with Ũ_< ⊆ J^±(S). An ETT form for 'achronal and met by every inextensible causal curve' would need push-up and a one-sided re-proof of the Cauchy lemma. It is not attempted.

Reading 3, 'past directed causal curve in Ũ starting below the graph' is read as C.dual.CausalCurveOn U c a b with c a ∈ V, over a segment. The future-parameter form (a future curve of Ũ ending in V) and, for the past chart, the form over any interval are proved too, so nothing is decided between them.

Then futureInextensible_of_leaving applies with the larger open W ⊔ Ũ, since it asks W ≤ U (T-abs-boundary-chart-cauchy).

A causal curve of W whose points lie in J⁻(S, W) is constant after it meets the Cauchy surface S, by acausality (eq_of_le_of_t1_secondCountable) and antisymmetry. This replaces Sbierski's 'I⁺(Σ) ∩ Σ = ∅', which ETT cannot use because ≪ is not irreflexive by axiom (T-abs-boundary-chart-cauchy).
